title: Madhava's infinite series for pi
summary: Madhava, founder of the Kerala school, derived infinite series for trigonometric functions and pi, centuries before similar results in Europe.
why: Infinite series are a foundation of calculus.

notes.problem: 'Little known outside Kerala' is not in the source; source only says Whish 'was the first to draw attention to their priority over Newton'.

unsung.contribution: Derived infinite series for pi and trigonometric functions around 1400.
unsung.recognition: A 19th-century paper by Charles Whish was the first to draw attention to the Kerala school's priority over Newton.
